narrative.overview: This system looks like a working analyst's desk: a cool paper-white surface, ink-dark text, hairline rules separating sections the way a desk blotter separates documents, and exactly one accent — a restrained cobalt blue — reserved for actions, active states, and emphasis. Nothing is decorative for its own sake. Every visual element either carries evidence (a metric, a screenshot, a tech tag) or organizes it (a border, a section eyebrow, a numbered index). Depth is structural, never theatrical: surfaces sit flat at rest and are separated by 1px borders; the only shadow in the entire system is a barely-there lift on card hover. Density is calm and reading-first, with numbered mono index chips, uppercase micro-labels, and tabular-figure metrics giving the site the annotated feel of a well-kept technical record.
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces + hairline borders as the primary separation mechanism.
One accent color (Restrained Cobalt) that signals only action/state/emphasis.
Two font families only: DM Sans for everything human-readable, DM Mono for technical annotation.
Numbered entries, uppercase eyebrow labels, and tabular metrics — the vocabulary of a working document.
Gentle curves everywhere (4px controls, 8px cards); pills only for role badges.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Restrained Cobalt means 'act, active, or emphasize' and nothing else. If an element is neither interactive, state-marked, nor a deliberate emphasis, it does not get cobalt.

rules.name: The Not-Teal, Not-Purple Rule
rules.body: The accent is cobalt, full stop. No teal, no violet, no blue→purple gradients — the source comment prohibits them and the system holds.

rules.name: The Two-Family Rule
rules.body: DM Sans and DM Mono only. No third font, no decorative face; hierarchy is built from weight and size, not novelty.

rules.name: The Mono Means Machine Rule
rules.body: Monospace appears only on technical annotation — tags, indices, code, data volumes. Never for body prose or headings.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders separate, shadows never do. Any new surface gets a 1px Hairline border first; a shadow needs a state (hover) to exist at all.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: There is no rest-state shadow in this system. Do not introduce one.

dos: Do separate surfaces with 1px Hairline borders and tonal fills (Snow/Fog/Cobalt Wash) before considering any shadow.
Do reserve Restrained Cobalt for actions, active states, links, and emphasis — and cap filled cobalt to one primary CTA per action row.
Do use DM Mono only for technical annotation: tags, indices, data volumes, code.
Do keep the page skeleton identical: bordered header band → eyebrow labels → bordered cards at 24px padding → single primary CTA row.
Do use dashed hairline borders for honest-absence states (private repo, in development) — the style encodes the honesty policy.
Do run numerals tabular (tabular-nums) and keep the 2px-offset cobalt focus ring on every interactive element.
Do update both :root and .dark token blocks together; every light token has a dark counterpart.
donts: Don't introduce gradients, glassmorphism (outside the header blur), glow effects, or rest-state shadows.
Don't add teal, violet, or blue→purple accent schemes; the accent is cobalt and the source comment forbids the drift.
Don't add a third font family or use uppercase mono as decorative chrome.
Don't widen body copy past the reading container (max-w-4xl) or shrink it below the 0.875rem document scale for 'style.'
Don't turn role-badge pills into a general chip shape; pills are for roles/status only.
Don't replace numbered index chips, section eyebrows, or the project-card layout with generic card grids — they are the desk's organizing system.
